Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 2 marks

steps.label: True breeding defined
steps.margin_note: Definition with self pollination and homozygous. Four lines.
lines: A TRUE BREEDING line is one that, after continuous
SELF POLLINATION, shows the same trait in every
It is homozygous for that trait.
steps.why: Only a homozygote can breed true, because it has just one kind of allele to pass on.
common_mistakes: Saying true breeding means cross pollination. It is produced by continuous SELF pollination.
Leaving out homozygous. Being homozygous is what makes a line breed true.
steps.memory_tip: Self it long enough and only one allele is left.

steps.label: Significance
steps.margin_note: Stability plus why an experimenter needs it. Five lines.

lines.text: A known, unchanging starting point for a cross

lines: It shows STABLE inheritance and expression of a
True breeding lines give an experimenter parents
of KNOWN genotype, which is what Mendel needed
steps.why: Without pure parents the F1 would already be mixed, and no ratio in F2 could be interpreted.
common_mistakes: Giving no significance. It is a whole mark.
Saying it produces variation. True breeding produces the OPPOSITE — uniformity.
steps.memory_tip: You cannot read the result unless you knew what went in.
